source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-81: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 81 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume the collective uses RoCE, but verify GPU/NIC/PCIe/NVLink affinity, direct-GPU versus host staging, software and firmware, link speed, MTU, VLAN/priority, PFC/ECN, routes, queue pairs, memory registration, message/concurrency mix, placement, clocks, and actual transport or fallback. Hypothesis: asymmetric routing or priority-class congestion creates unstable upper quantiles; host scheduling and workload drift are alternatives. Begin with authorized read-only inventory and synchronized application, verbs, NIC, and switch evidence. Measure p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency in ms, throughput, retries, completion errors, timeouts, drops, ECN, queue depth and PFC pauses over equal-size interleaved baseline and treatment samples, reporting sample counts and uncertainty. Any change requires owner approval, one-variable canary, known-good snapshot, correctness checks, and rollback on preset tail, timeout, drop, pause, or correctness thresholds.
